role.altitude: The two accountants spend less time pulling AFAS reports into Excel and building tie-outs by hand. They spend more on writing the checks, mapping tables and thresholds that test every balance, and on the few variances, tax positions and estimates that need judgement. They sign off on the close and the annual file. They do not rebuild them.
reach: Controller: own the month-close checklist and the audit file together, so audit adjustments fall.
FP&A Analyst: share one driver model for flex labour and revenue, so the forecast and the close use the same numbers.
Bookkeeper: feed the AP and AR exception rules (duplicates, IBAN changes, agency invoice mismatches) from what the balance review finds.
skills_to_grow: Writing and testing reconciliation rules and tie-out checks in SQL or Python on the AFAS extract
Reviewing model-drafted variance explanations and spotting unstated assumptions
Dutch tax positions (VAT reverse charge, Vpb fiscal differences) explained in a form an auditor can rebuild
Preparing for e-invoicing and SBR filing to KVK
role.ambitious_version: Every balance sheet account is reconciled and checked every night, not once a month, against AFAS, Rabobank CAMT.053 and the agency portals. The accountants review only the breaks. The close drops from days to a sign-off. The year-end file arrives at the auditor already tied out, with each figure traced to its source.

tasks.short: Monthly review of balance sheet and P&L balances in AFAS for odd movements before close sign-off.

steps.what: Export trial balance and subledger reports from AFAS into Excel
Compare balances to prior month, budget and account reconciliations
Investigate odd movements in journal lines, invoices and with bookkeepers

loop.input: Variance above threshold plus the journal lines, descriptions and linked invoices behind it
loop.output: Draft explanation naming the journal lines that cause the movement
loop.check: Amounts of the cited lines must add up to the variance within a set tolerance; each line id must exist in AFAS
loop.stop: One draft and up to two retries per variance; if the tie-out fails it is marked 'unexplained' for the accountant
loop.why_not_simpler: Journal descriptions and invoice texts are free text; rules alone cannot name the cause of a movement

steps.what: Write review notes and sign off to the controller

tasks.design: A nightly Python job on a governed data platform reads AFAS trial balance and subledgers through GetConnectors. It compares every account with prior month, budget and its reconciliation, and feeds a Power BI review page that flags breaks above a threshold. A bounded model step drafts an explanation per flagged variance, tied out to journal lines. The accountant accepts or rewrites it, and the sign-off note is generated from the accepted explanations.
tasks.previous_blocker: The review lived in Excel exports rebuilt each month. Explaining a movement needed someone to read journal texts and invoices.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the AFAS extract and checks cheap to build. Models can read journal descriptions and draft explanations that a sum check can verify.
tasks.still_hard: Judging whether a correct explanation is also acceptable, for example an accrual that is right in amount but wrong in period. Thresholds need tuning so the list stays short.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the business behind a number: a lost customer, a season peak in flex workers, a one-off claim. Deciding whether a movement is a booking error or a real event.

ambition.what: Balance review runs every night during the close, not once at month end, so errors are fixed while the period is still open.

tasks.altitude: The accountant opens a short break list each morning of the close, not a workbook. They gain the right to set and change variance thresholds per account together with the controller.

reach.learn: Which variances the controller always asks about, so they get a standing rule
Which coding errors cause most balance breaks, to fix them at entry

evidence.claim: Models beat experienced CPAs on month-end tasks that reward detail and file search, but not on client questions and tacit context
Multi-step reasoning across files causes over half of top-model errors on accounting tasks
A model that adds an unnoticed assumption makes a workpaper impossible to rebuild
AFAS GetConnectors expose ledger data for a scheduled extract

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract for Power BI can be extended with journal lines and reconciliations
Account reconciliations are kept in a fixed format per account
unknowns: How many balance sheet accounts are reconciled monthly today
Whether a governed data platform exists beyond the Power BI extract
research_questions: What share of last year's flagged variances could be explained from journal descriptions alone?
How many variances per close pass a threshold of, say, 5% and EUR 10,000?
Does the auditor accept a generated sign-off note with line references as evidence?

tasks.short: Work out Noordhaven's VAT returns and corporate tax provision, including depreciation and fiscal differences.

steps.what: Pull VAT code totals and ledger balances from AFAS
Reconcile VAT accounts to return; check reverse-charge, intra-EU and agency invoices
Compute corporate tax provision: depreciation, fiscal differences, interest, deferred tax
Check return with Jonas and adviser, then file with the tax office

tasks.design: Configure the AFAS VAT return and Jonas checks in Profit. Add a scheduled Python job that tests every purchase and sales line for VAT code consistency: reverse charge on foreign suppliers, intra-EU sales, and agency invoices against portal amounts. Exceptions go into a short list. A generated provision workbook rolls fiscal depreciation and fiscal differences forward from the prior year. The accountant sets the estimates, and the controller approves them before anything is filed.
tasks.previous_blocker: VAT checks were spot checks in Excel because testing every line by hand was too slow. Tax positions depend on judgement and carry legal risk.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS Jonas now assists with VAT and corporate tax returns in Profit. Rule tests over all lines are cheap to write with AI coding.
tasks.still_hard: Estimates and positions such as deductibility, fiscal valuations and provisions. They must stay human-approved, and Jonas leaves responsibility with the user.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing and defending a tax position, weighing risk with the adviser, and dealing with the Belastingdienst.

ambition.what: VAT code checks run on every booked line each week, not once per return, so wrong codes are fixed before filing.

tasks.altitude: The accountant reviews an exception list and the positions, not raw totals. They gain the right to set the VAT test rules that bookkeepers' postings must pass.

reach.learn: Which suppliers and agencies most often get the wrong VAT code
What documentation the controller and auditor need per position

evidence.claim: AFAS Jonas assists in VAT returns from 2026 and in corporate tax returns; the user stays responsible for the check
Tax estimates belong on the mandatory human review list
Intra-EU and reverse-charge e-invoicing rules are coming; domestic B2B from 1 July 2030, not yet law

assumptions: Noordhaven files VAT itself through AFAS and uses an external adviser for the corporate tax return
Fixed asset register is in AFAS
unknowns: Profit version and whether Jonas tax features are licensed
Role split with the external tax adviser
research_questions: How many VAT code corrections did last year's returns and audit find?
Do Jonas checks catch the reverse-charge cases Noordhaven sees on agency and foreign carrier invoices?
Will the adviser accept a generated provision workbook as their starting file?

tasks.short: Prepare and check the annual report, monthly statements and notes from AFAS for controller and auditor.

steps.what: Collect closing trial balance, adjusting entries and supporting schedules
Map ledger accounts to statement lines and notes
Build statements, note tables and tie-out checks
Draft notes text and analysis of financial condition

loop.input: Current and prior year note tables, prior year note text, key movements
loop.output: Updated note text with each figure as a placeholder linked to the table
loop.check: Every number in the text is rendered from the table, not typed by the model; a script rejects any free-typed figure
loop.stop: One draft per note, one retry; on failure the prior year text is carried over and marked for rewrite
loop.why_not_simpler: Rolling forward narrative text after changes needs reading and rewriting prose

steps.what: Answer controller and auditor questions; finalize for KVK filing

tasks.design: Keep a maintained account-to-line mapping table in a small app on the data platform. A Python generator then builds the monthly and annual statements, note tables and a tie-out report straight from the AFAS closing data. A bounded model step rolls note text forward, and every number in it is linked to a table cell. The controller approves, the auditor gets the tie-out file, and filing to KVK via SBR goes through a separate tool or the auditor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mapping and note tables were rebuilt in Excel each year, and text and figures drifted apart. Building a generator for one annual report did not seem worth it.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a statement generator a few days' work. Models can roll text forward when figures stay under code control.
tasks.still_hard: Judgement items: provisions, impairments, classifications and disclosures under Dutch GAAP, which no benchmark tests. SBR filing to KVK is not covered by AFAS.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding presentation and disclosure, and defending choices to the auditor and the Finance Director.

ambition.what: A monthly mini balance sheet and P&L pack in annual report format, with tie-out, for the Finance Director and site managers.

tasks.altitude: The accountant reviews generated statements and spends the freed hours on judgement items and auditor questions. They gain ownership of the mapping table and the tie-out rules.

reach.learn: Which tie-outs the auditor asks for every year, so they are generated by default
Use the same mapping so management and statutory figures match

evidence.claim: Large companies file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025; AFAS cannot file this for them
On 160 GAAP tasks the leading model meets 61.8% of criteria; judgement is the bottleneck
Workday's agent prepares entries for review, teams stay responsible
Accountants using AI closed 7.5 days faster across 79 firms

assumptions: Noordhaven counts as a large company for KVK filing
Statements are prepared in-house and audited externally
unknowns: Which tool or party files with KVK via SBR today
Whether monthly statements are formal or management-only
How many audit adjustments came from mapping or tie-out errors last year
research_questions: How many hours did last year's annual report take from trial balance to auditor-ready draft?
Does the auditor accept a generated tie-out report in place of the Excel file?
Can the account mapping be held stable across two years without manual fixes?

tasks.short: Analyze cost and revenue trends, such as flex labour and customer revenue, to project figures and advise management.

steps.what: Gather actuals, agency invoices and revenue by customer and site
Build trend and cost driver analysis in Excel
Project revenue and expenses for coming months
Write advice memo with findings and options

loop.input: Top driver movements and projection versus budget, as tables
loop.check: Figures are inserted from the tables; a script checks each claim's direction (up or down) against the data
loop.stop: One draft and one retry per section; otherwise the section stays as a table only
loop.why_not_simpler: Readable commentary is free text; templates read poorly once more than a few drivers move

steps.what: Discuss findings with controller and site managers

tasks.design: Extend the nightly AFAS extract with agency portal hours and invoices, and build Power BI pages for cost drivers: flex hours and rates per site, transport cost per order, revenue per customer. A Python job produces a driver-based baseline projection. A bounded model step drafts commentary with figures inserted from the tables. The accountant adjusts the projection and the memo, then advises in person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agency portal data never reached AFAS in usable form, so analyses were one-off Excel builds. Commentary was written from scratch each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Portal exports and AFAS connectors can be joined cheaply with AI-built code. Models draft commentary well when figures are under code control.
tasks.still_hard: Projections depend on business events: contracts won or lost, seasonal peaks, CAO wage rounds. The data does not contain these. Forecast errors only show later.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what is about to change in the business and turning numbers into advice site managers trust.

ambition.what: A monthly flex labour cost view per site for the three site managers, who today get only total cost.

tasks.altitude: The accountant moves from building analyses to questioning them and advising managers. They gain a regular seat in site cost reviews.

reach.learn: Which drivers FP&A uses, so accountant projections feed the forecast directly
Planned flex volumes per season, an input the ledger cannot show

evidence.claim: Leaving out client communication and tacit context is where models fall short in accounting work
Commentary on budget against actual fits deterministic software plus a model step
Accountants using AI closed faster and served more clients; most worry about errors

assumptions: All three agency portals offer an export or API for hours and invoices
Site-level cost centres exist in AFAS
unknowns: Whether flex-worker hours data per person needs works council consent or a DPIA under AVG
Agency contract terms on data use
How the accountant and FP&A split forecasting work today
research_questions: Can the three agency portals deliver hours and invoices in a stable format each week?
How accurate was last year's flex cost projection, and what drove the misses?
Do site managers use a per-site cost view if it is offered?
